en: I eat bread.
why: object before the action, as Real SASL teaches and its Deaf presenters sign; ME EAT BREAD (Wehrmeyer 2025) is the other order

en: I want to learn sign language.
why: WANT first, then what is learnt, then the action (Wright 2017: SHOULD SCHOOL NORTH-WEST GO); 'to' is not signed

en: I want you to come.
why: who you want to come sits between the two verbs, as in English

en: I need to buy milk and bread.
gloss: ME NEED MILK AND BREAD BUY
alt: ME NEED BUY MILK AND BREAD
why: NEED first, then the things, then the action they need doing (helper; object before the action)

en: I forgot to call my mother.
gloss: PAST ME FORGET MY MOTHER CALL
alt: PAST ME FORGET CALL MY MOTHER
why: CALL moves toward the mother, so she comes right before CALL (directional); FORGET stays before them

en: You should go to school.
why: place early; SHOULD last, as the DBE Grade 12 exams sign modals (the one SASL thesis example, Wright 2017, has SHOULD first)

en: I have a cat and a dog.
why: HAVE comes last in every SASL source example (Real SASL: ME HOUSE WHITE BIG TWO HAVE)

en: I like chocolate.
why: LIKE comes last (Real SASL: ANIMALS LIKE)

en: I put the keys on the table.
why: a verb that moves a thing to a place comes last, after the thing and the place (Napoli & Sutton-Spence 2014: WOMAN BOX TABLE PUT-ON)

en: I think it will rain tomorrow.
why: ME THINK, then the second idea with its own time; TOMORROW belongs to the rain, so it does not open the sentence

en: I hope you feel better.
why: HOPE, then the second idea in its own order

en: I know that she is sick.
why: 'that' joining two ideas is not signed

en: She told me that she is tired.
why: TELL moves from her to me; then what she said

en: She is taller than her sister.
why: set up the sister, then her, then TALL MORE (Wright 2017: comparison with MORE between two spaces); THAN is not signed

en: He runs faster than me.
why: the other side first, then who, the action, FAST MORE

en: I have lived here for ten years.
why: how long is a time and opens the sentence; the number goes with the time sign (CAPS numeral incorporation: TWO WEEKS); still true now, so no PAST

en: I have been learning SASL for two months.
why: how long first; still going on, so no PAST; SASL is fingerspelled

en: We stayed in Durban for a week.
gloss: PAST ONE WEEK DURBAN WE STAY
why: finished in the past, so PAST is added before how long it lasted

en: I usually eat breakfast at seven.
gloss: TIME SEVEN ME USUALLY BREAKFAST EAT
alt: TIME SEVEN ME USUALLY EAT BREAKFAST
why: a clock time in words is a time: TIME SEVEN opens the sentence

en: I wake up at six o'clock.
why: TIME and the hour; o'clock is not signed

en: I work from Monday to Friday.
why: the two days are the time and go first

en: After school I go home.
why: AFTER SCHOOL is a time and opens the sentence

en: I went to the movies on Friday.
why: where you go sets the scene, whatever the place; 'to' is not signed (Real SASL: SHOP ME GO)

en: We watched two movies.
why: movies is MOVIE, then how many

en: I saw a beautiful bird in the tree.
gloss: PAST TREE ME BIRD BEAUTIFUL SEE
alt: PAST TREE ME SEE BIRD BEAUTIFUL
why: the place sets the scene; then who, the action, the thing

en: The ball is in the box.
why: the box first, the ball, then IN (CAPS: basic prepositions; set up the ground first)

en: I talked to my teacher about the test.
gloss: PAST ME MY TEACHER TALK ABOUT TEST
alt: PAST ME TALK MY TEACHER ABOUT TEST
why: the person you talk to follows the verb; 'to' is not signed

en: She drove to work by car.
why: the car follows the action; 'by' is not signed

en: She is twenty years old.
why: AGE and the number (Wright 2017: AGE SIX)

en: Thank you very much.
why: one THANK-YOU, signed with more emphasis

en: The man who lives next door is deaf.
why: 'who' is not signed; the man, what he does, then what he is

en: What are you doing?
why: DO is a real sign (Real SASL verbs lesson); question word last
